grh_779b685899c973fc064f.title: The Headless Monk
paragraphs: Holmes accompanies occult investigator Harley to a Cornish manor where an old chapel is said to be haunted by a headless monk and ghostly organ music. Harley concludes that someone is using the legend to conceal black-magic rites, and he is later stabbed inside the chapel while standing within a protective pentagram. A stableman insists no mortal entered, but admits seeing the headless ghost. Holmes realizes the disguise must have raised false shoulders above the wearer's hidden head, making the apparent height misleading. The culprit is Dorothy Brownlee, the owner's daughter, who created the haunting so she could practice black magic undisturbed and killed Harley when he threatened to expose her. She flees toward the organ loft and falls to her death.

This [[show|the-new-adventures-of-sherlock-holmes|The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes]] broadcast aired on April 15, 1946. [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Basil Rathbone and Nigel Bruce. Other credited names include Edna Best as producer and Harry Bartell as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]] and [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]].
This version is based on [[work|work.doyle.6c28d2e9a5bfb8b6|The Adventure of the Devil's Foot]]. Arthur Conan Doyle is credited as author.

grh_778070cd9a960ccc1572.title: Swan Lake
paragraphs: American tourist Richard Sims becomes enchanted by ballerina Tanya Graciana after seeing her dance in London, never realizing that the ordinary American woman who keeps crossing his path is Tanya herself under her real identity, Thelma Green. grh_7724b0c49181b9c8aaa6.title: Gunners Get Glory
paragraphs: Navy armed-guard officer Bob Berry recalls being rushed through wartime training and sent to defend merchant ships against submarine and air attack. His service includes the sinking of a ship, hours in an oil-covered sea and survival in a lifeboat with other crewmen while they ration food, water and cigarettes. Berry eventually returns home, physically safe but marked by what happened at sea. When friends invite him and his wife to a swimming party, the idea is unbearable, and the story closes with the couple awaiting the birth of their child.
